headline: Learned models rank enzyme, reaction and mutant candidates, with benchmarks and wet-lab checks
label: Learned Enzyme Candidate Prioritization
summary: New enzyme-ranking models are paired with campaign-grouped benchmarks, reaction-disjoint tests and experimental validation, tightening how prioritization is assessed.
synthesis: The common thread is learned prioritization of enzyme-related candidates: enzyme-reaction pairs (RIVER), kcat and Km (KineCouple, AlphaEnzyme), active versus decoy enzymes and EC numbers (DecoyOpt), fungal peroxygenase substrates, and mutants (EnzyArena). Several methods build on pretrained protein or molecule encoders, such as frozen ProtT5/MolT5 in KineCouple and ESM3-generated decoys in DecoyOpt. The newer emphasis is evaluation and validation. EnzyArena groups kinetic data by campaign, compares 20 models, finds zero-shot consensus best, and tests 150 mutants. The generative-reaction study uses a reaction-disjoint benchmark, and the peroxygenase workflow combines mining, wet-lab screening and gradient-boosting models. The items differ in task and scope, so this is a shared direction rather than one method.
